_README: Curated laws for ds_contract, merged onto the primitive it names. Absence of an entry means nobody has written the law yet — NOT that anything is permitted. Keep this small: a rule here is a rule an agent will follow, and a stale one is worse than none. Every entry cites where the decision was taken.

DeskStageOverlay.useWhen: desk record form, L2 multi-field edit, Center Lock, stage overlay, order intake stage fill, fill the desk-page-stage, full width full height form over the table, stage-filling L2, edit a row on the desk table
DeskStageOverlay.doNot: Do not mount a viewport Dialog, RightPaneOverlay, or DeskRecordWalkHost XOR for desk record editing (Q5). Do not invent a second overlay host. `fill="inset"` is a padded max-measure card; `fill="stage"` covers the entire desk-page-stage card edge-to-edge like DataTable (DESK_TABLE_SURFACE_CLASS) — use stage for intake / long triage forms that must not read as a popover. Never pass max-w-* on stage fill. Table stays mounted underneath. Body is TriageScrollLayout; reading measure is inside the form, not the shell.
DeskStageOverlay.law: src/design-system/components/DeskStageOverlay.tsx + docs/warehouse-os/PLAN-center-lock.md + LAWS.md Q5. Operator 2026-09-02: fill=stage for Order intake.

DeskStageContext.useWhen: fullscreen, expand the table, stage state, is this table on a desk, desk stage, maximize the grid
DeskStageContext.doNot: Do not add a second fullscreen state or a second toggle. DeskPageChrome OWNS the state and publishes it here; the control lives on the table's own toolbar row (DataTableFullscreenToggle), which renders NOTHING when useDeskStageOptional() is null — a station embed or a modal-hosted table has no stage to expand, and a dead control is worse than no control. Do not move the toggle up to the page header: in fullscreen that header is not rendered.
DeskStageContext.law: src/design-system/components/DeskStageContext.tsx. Operator 2026-08-30: the fullscreen control belongs on the table's row, not the page's.

DeskActionSlot.useWhen: page CTA, primary action on a desk, overall action, leading action, Labels left of Sync, Labels display toggle, Export in the Sync dropdown, register an action into the page header, Add button on a workbench, desk action slot
DeskActionSlot.doNot: Do not pass a CTA down as a prop through the route-group layout — a shared frame that imports one desk's intake stops being shared. The active surface registers with DeskActionSlotRegistrar (role=primary for the create verb, role=overall for collection actions such as Media Export, role=leading for To-ship Labels immediately left of primary). Last writer wins per role, so Labels does not replace Add. A desk with no CTA registers nothing and the slot stays empty. Memoize the node — a fresh element identity every render re-registers every render, which loops through the provider. The node is DeskHeaderAction (Button with radius pill locked) or SlicedActionDock embeddedChrome=header for a split intake — never a raw Button with a rounded-* class, never radius flush in this slot. Print, filter, columns, zoom and fullscreen stay off this row. To-ship Export is not an overall header button — DeskExportMenuRegistrar tucks it into the Sync Google Sheet dropdown (operator 2026-09-01). Labels is a display toggle for the paperwork walk (pressed = walk on), not a per-row print verb.
DeskActionSlot.law: src/design-system/components/DeskActionSlot.tsx. Operator 2026-08-30: the CTA is page-level, top-right of the header. Operator 2026-09-01: every desk header CTA uses the same pill token (DeskHeaderAction / SlicedActionDock header chrome); a per-page corner is a fork. Operator 2026-09-01: overall actions (Export) sit in the header cluster left of the primary CTA on desks that still own a collection Export; To-ship tucks Export into the Sync dropdown. Operator 2026-09-01: To-ship Labels is role=leading, immediately left of Sync, and toggles the paperwork display.

KeyboardKey.useWhen: keyboard keycap, hotkey glyph, teaching key, cheat sheet kbd, shortcut chip, physical key face, selection CTA hotkey overlay, chord in a tooltip
KeyboardKey.doNot: Do not hand-roll a second `<kbd>` face for teaching chords. On page chrome (tone=default) do not paint bg-surface-canvas (white) or text-text-muted (gray letter) — gray sunken face + black letter only. On an inverse surface do not use tone=default: a light cap on a dark chip out-shouts the sentence it explains. Never fold a chord into label text ('Switch mode Shift + Tab') — KeyboardChord splits it into caps. Scan-hotkey bind-edit and faint menu-trailing hints are not this job.
KeyboardKey.law: src/design-system/primitives/KeyboardKey.tsx. Operator 2026-09-01: one physical keycap SoT — bg-surface-sunken + text-text-default. TableStatusBar HotkeyGlyph overlays size=sm absolute right-1.5; cheat sheets use size=md. Operator 2026-09-05: tones are the ground the cap sits on — tone=inverse (tooltip chips) is darker than its chip (bg-scrim/40), light hairline (border-glass/20), dimmed letter (text-text-inverse-soft), no lift, size=xs. Case, weight and tracking are TONE decisions, never shared: default shouts (uppercase, font-semibold, tracking-widest), inverse does not (normal-case, font-medium, tracking-normal) — operator 2026-09-06, caps in a tooltip read 'Shift' and 'Tab', never 'SHIFT'. KeyboardChord({chord}) is the only way to render a whole chord and defaults to xs+inverse.

HotkeyTooltip.useWhen: teach a shortcut on hover, hotkey in tooltip, mode switcher hint, shift tab hint, what does this control do, chord hint, replace a standing keyboard-hint row
HotkeyTooltip.doNot: Do not print a chord as permanent chrome under a surface (a row that reads 'Shift + Tab' below the composer) — the hint belongs under the pointer. Do not build a tooltip that restates the control's own visible label: a face reading 'Unbox' gains nothing from a bubble reading 'Unbox' — render no tooltip instead. Do not pass a noun as `action`; it is a verb phrase ('Switch mode'). Do not reach for HoverTooltip+shortcut directly when teaching a chord, and do not re-implement cursor-chip vs bubble routing.
HotkeyTooltip.law: src/components/ui/HotkeyTooltip.tsx. Operator 2026-09-05: one SoT for 'what this does + the key that does it'. Both `action` and `chord` are REQUIRED, so the API cannot express a label-echo tooltip. Composes HoverTooltip (routing: cursor chip on a fine pointer, anchored role=tooltip bubble for focus/touch/reduced motion) and TooltipChip (skin + content order). Chords are authored as one display string beside the behaviour that owns them (STATION_COMPOSER_CYCLE_CHORD), never re-typed at the call site. First adopter: the composer mode row. Operator 2026-09-06: EVERY face of a switcher teaches the chord, selected or not — only one chip is ever on screen because it rides the pointer, so it is the same answer wherever the hand asks, not the same key printed N times. The faces still publish no cursor label of their own.

HoverTooltip.useWhen: hover help text, explain a control, what does this mean, meaning of a grade or status, tooltip on a pill, follow the mouse tooltip, native title replacement, tooltip copy style, tooltip dwell delay
HoverTooltip.doNot: Do not hand-roll a positioned tooltip div, do not add a second tooltip primitive (the vendored Radix `ui/tooltip.tsx` was DELETED 2026-09-06 — it was a fourth skin in raw shadcn vocabulary, zero call sites, and its `--foreground` ground is not even defined here), and do not leave a bare `title` attribute as the only explanation — the browser tip is slow, unstyled, and unthemable (the cursor layer lifts short titles onto the chip, but authoring one is not the pattern; the ratchet is components/ui/native-title.test.ts). Do not author a hover vocabulary where some entries fit the ride cap and others do not: the strip then has two behaviours and the operator sees a pointer-following chip on one pill and a static bubble on the next. Do not push prose through a hint — two sentences belong in the anchored bubble or a panel, not on a moving pointer. Do not end a hint FRAGMENT with a period, and do not author the same sentence twice in two files — extract it (ZONE_LETTER_UNASSIGNED_HINT, CONDITION_DESCRIPTIONS). Do not add a dwell delay to a normal control.
HoverTooltip.law: src/components/ui/HoverTooltip.tsx — the ONE hint primitive; there is no other. One trigger, two destinations, chosen by the runtime and never by the call site: a MOUSE hover on a desk hands the label to MorphCursorLayer via useCursorLabel (one chip that follows the pointer); focus, touch, reduced motion, rich/multi-line labels and anything past CURSOR_LABEL_MAX_CHARS keep the anchored role=tooltip bubble. Operator 2026-09-06: cap raised 48 -> 72 in src/design-system/motion/cursor-label.ts because the chip is now one nowrap row of 13px role-nav that flips at the viewport edges. That ported 25 more static labels app-wide (258 of 270 now ride) and un-split the condition-grade vocabulary, where Like new / Refurbished / Used A / Used B had been overshooting the old cap by 1-7 characters while their three siblings followed the pointer. Vocabularies must ride as a SET — guarded by cursor-label.test.ts 'a hover vocabulary rides as ONE'. Descriptions live in src/lib/conditions.ts CONDITION_DESCRIPTIONS, never inline at a call site. COPY: a hint is a fragment in sentence case with NO terminal period (measured 2026-09-06: 260 of 271 static labels already follow this); the period belongs to prose sentences in the bubble. conditionDescription() is the one sanctioned exception — it is dual-purpose, rendered as dialog body text in BulkConditionDialog where the period is correct. DWELL: instant is the default and openDelayMs is for TRANSIT paths only — a control the pointer crosses on its way somewhere else. Exactly one adopter, HorizontalEdgeResizeHandle at 1500ms; adding a delay anywhere else just makes the app feel slow.

TooltipChip.useWhen: tooltip skin, hover hint paint, cursor chip, tooltip bubble, copy tooltip, hint type size, chord placement in a tooltip, tooltip ground, tooltip corner radius
TooltipChip.doNot: Do not re-declare the chip skin in a host: no bg-surface-inverse, no type role of your own, no gap/padding of your own, and never reach past TooltipChipBody to KeyboardChord. Do not put the chord before the sentence. Do not use text-role-micro or text-role-eyebrow for a hint — both bind the CONDENSED family and a hint must be legible on first read. Do not Title Case or shout a hint — sentence case, always. Do not let a hint wrap: never pass `wrap` from the cursor chip, and never cap the width of a no-wrap chip (the sentence would overflow its own ground). Do not make a CLICKABLE hint follow the pointer — a copy or open-link target the hand has to enter must hold still. Do not paint a hint flush-square: the flush ruling covers welded instrument chrome, not floating hints.
TooltipChip.law: src/design-system/primitives/TooltipChip.tsx. Operator 2026-09-06: a hint has THREE hosts and they all paint this skin — the desk chip on MorphCursorLayer (rides the pointer), the anchored bubble in HoverTooltip, and the anchored copy bubble in SiteTooltipProvider. A host owns POSITION and its corner role only; ground, type, row spacing and content order come from tooltipChipClass()/TooltipChipBody so they cannot drift. `row` means a trailing element (keycaps, a copy glyph) sits beside the sentence; `wrap` is a bubble-only opt-in. Type is text-role-nav at font-medium — 13px on the app sans cut, zero tracking, the most legible cut available, NOT the smallest (the small/condensed pass was reversed the same day: a tip is read by someone who does not yet know what the control does). px-2 py-1, gap-1.5; the chord goes AFTER the sentence because the reader wants what before how. ONE ROW is the default. CORNER: cornerClass('control') on the cursor chip and the copy bubble — the copy shell's earlier flush-square ruling ('ops density; floating is not a soft-radius escape') is REVERSED for hints, because a square copy bubble reads as a different surface from the rounded chip. Guarded by cursor-label.test.ts 'one skin, one content order'.

TableStatusBar.useWhen: row count, shown of total, selected count, copy selection, table foot strip, sub-mode tabs inside one page tab, selection CTA hotkey reveal, idle-left path readout lead
TableStatusBar.doNot: Do not wire NEW page modes into its `tabs` props. Page modes ride DeskPageChrome's TOP row on every desk AND every scan station (operator 2026-08-31) — the desk-threaded `tabStrip` plumbing was deleted the same day. What this strip is for is the right half (shown / total / selected / copy), which is the one thing a table knows and a frame does not; its tab half survives only for SECOND-level sub-modes inside a single page tab. Idle-left `lead` is a context readout (date/folder path) — never a CTA, never page navigation, never painted beside selection pills (precedence: selectionActions beat tabs beat lead). `lead` is not DeskPageChrome's `tabsLead`. Do not hand-roll a teaching `<kbd>` for selection hotkeys — mount KeyboardKey. Do not leave standing letters, open a cheat sheet from staff `?` while CTAs are mounted, add a foot `?`, park keycaps outside, or widen via iconRight/gap.
TableStatusBar.law: src/components/tables/TableStatusBar.tsx. Operator 2026-08-31: tabs moved to the top; the foot strip keeps the counts. Operator 2026-09-01: keyboard `?` reveals KeyboardKey overlays inside each CTA (absolute right-1.5), gray face + black letter, zero layout shift. Operator 2026-09-01: `lead` fills the idle left for Media path contraction.

DeskPageChrome.useWhen: page header, page title, page-level primary action, in-page tabs, workbench frame, desk frame, non-scan desk, fixed-width stage, detached table card, table fullscreen, comfortable desk display, breathable desk, airy desk, desk profile, card on canvas, pleasing desk layout
DeskPageChrome.doNot: ALWAYS the desk measure — there is no edge-to-edge mode and no `bleed` prop (added and removed 2026-09-01). Edge-to-edge belongs to the BENCH compositions (StationWorkbench / StationPanelRoot / PackOrderPanel / LineEditPanel / TriagePanel), which do not mount this frame at all. A scan station's BROWSE side imports desk tables (ReceivingLinesTable, TechAllTriageTable, UnshippedTable) and a desk table wears the desk measure wherever it is mounted. Do not hand-roll a page title row, a tab strip, or a `max-w-*` stage on any non-scan desk. Scope: operator DESKS only — settings/admin pages and detail panels keep PageHeader from @/components/ui/pane-header, and a full-canvas surface (/studio) takes neither — this is the frame, and a second one is a fork. Scan stations mount it too (operator 2026-08-31) — /unbox, /pack, /test, /triage, /shipping/scan-out wear the same frame as the Shipping desk, and their mode tabs ride the TOP row, never a TableStatusBar foot strip. A station passes its tabs explicitly because they are body-switchers, not nav children. Do not pass a title literal — the title is nav data, threaded by @/components/desk/DeskPageLayout off the page's SIDEBAR_PAGE_NAV label, so the header cannot drift from the spine. Do not paint a Scan Stations peer chip in GlobalHeader — floor benches switch from MasterNav hover-peek; Recents is sessions only (operator 2026-09-01). Do not hand-roll tab alignment or add a first-tab padding exception. Use DESK_TAB_LIST_CLASS + DESK_TAB_TRIGGER_CLASS from src/design-system/tokens/desk-stage.ts: fixed-width triggers with centered labels are the shared desk primitive. Do not put intake CTAs (Sync, Add order) on the tab row — those stay in addSlot on the title row. `tabsLead` (start) and `tabsTrail` (end) are the tab row's same-axis slots for overflow of the tab vocabulary — not a second CTA and not a create-table plus. Desk tabs reorder by dragging those same triggers — not Studio, not MasterNav arrange. Do not use role-display for the title (role-title, 18px/600), do not animate the tab underline between tabs, and do not add a second measure token: DESK_STAGE_MAX_PX is the one desk width. `titleSlot` replaces the <h1> only where the page's identity IS the operator's own input (/search's query); a page with a NAME uses `title`. A row refinement goes on the table's toolbar. In fullscreen the header and tab row are NOT rendered — never re-parent the search or the fullscreen toggle, they already live on the table's own row in both states. Desk profile: capped centered stage + white ground + card welded to the tab row with no full-width hairline + rounded CARD SHELL only — DataTable stays edge-to-edge inside via DESK_TABLE_SURFACE_CLASS; never round the grid itself. Do not restore a mt-5 / mt-4 gap above the card. Do not restore a full-width border-b on DESK_TAB_ROW_CLASS.
DeskPageChrome.law: src/design-system/components/DeskPageChrome.tsx + src/design-system/components/DeskTab.tsx + src/design-system/tokens/desk-stage.ts. docs/todo/desk-page-header-industry-standard-HANDOFF.md — title · CTA · tabs · table card. Operator 2026-08-31: the chrome is the design system's, and every other page ports onto it. Operator 2026-09-01: DeskTab + DESK_TAB_LIST_CLASS + DESK_TAB_TRIGGER_CLASS are the shared fixed-width, centered-label tab primitive. Operator 2026-09-02: desk profile = breathable card shell; table flush inside. Operator 2026-09-04: no gap and no full-width hairline between tabs and table toolbar (DESK_STAGE_DETACH_CLASS empty; DESK_TAB_ROW_CLASS has no border-b). TableStatusBar has no border-t.

desk-stage.useWhen: desk stage tokens, desk profile, comfortable desk display, breathable desk, desk gutter, desk card shell, DESK_STAGE_MAX_PX, edge to edge table inside card, desk measure
desk-stage.doNot: Pointer-desk profile ONLY — scan stations use station-skin + cornerClass('flush'), not these tokens. Do not round DataTable — only DESK_CHROME_STAGE_BODY_CLASS on desk-page-stage carries radius; toolbar and grid use DESK_TABLE_SURFACE_CLASS (flush, rounded-none). Do not add a per-page max-w. Do not unify desk and scan-station chrome. Do not restore DESK_STAGE_DETACH_CLASS to mt-5 / mt-4 or DESK_TAB_ROW_CLASS to a full-width border-b — the card welds to the tab row.
desk-stage.law: src/design-system/tokens/desk-stage.ts — ds_tokens({ axis: 'desk-stage' }). Card shell is soft; table is edge-to-edge inside.

DeskTab.useWhen: fixed-width desk tab, centered tab label, desk mode switcher, page-mode tab, tab trigger inside DeskPageChrome, reorder desk tabs, drag desk tabs
DeskTab.doNot: Do not hand-roll a raw tab button inside a desk page. Do not add flex-1, a first-tab padding exception, or page-local alignment classes: DeskTab preserves intrinsic fixed-width sizing with shrink-0 and centers its label with the shared DESK_TAB_TRIGGER_CLASS. Keep routing and active state in the caller; this primitive owns the tab face, underline, focus ring, hover state and count presentation. Reorder happens on this tab row (hold-drag). Do not build a Studio canvas, a MasterNav arrange mode, or a second tab list to move desk tabs. Do not mint or delete tabs from drag.
DeskTab.law: src/design-system/components/DeskTab.tsx + src/design-system/tokens/desk-stage.ts. Operator 2026-09-01: extracted from DeskPageChrome so every desk mode label is centered without changing fixed tab sizing. Operator 2026-09-02: desk page tabs reorder inline on the TOP row — drag the tabs you already click.

DeskPageLayout.useWhen: desk route group layout, mount the desk frame, opt a page into desk chrome, workbench layout
DeskPageLayout.doNot: Not a design-system file (it reads SIDEBAR_PAGE_NAV / AuthContext, which the system must not import) — it lives at @/components/desk/DeskPageLayout. Do not copy its body into a domain layout: a domain gets `<DeskPageLayout>{children}</DeskPageLayout>` plus, at most, a `decorateTabs` callback for counts it can prove. Do not fetch through useQuery inside it — a route-group layout renders above the app QueryClientProvider.
DeskPageLayout.law: Operator 2026-08-31: one desk frame, ported to every non-scan page. Opt in with deskChrome: true on the page's SIDEBAR_PAGE_NAV entry.

Button.useWhen: ops CTA, action, submit, confirm, cancel, toolbar action, execute, success intent, anything an operator would call a button
Button.doNot: Do not hand-roll a <button> for an operator action. Do not use this for 21st.dev / shadcn-lane chrome — that is `button` from @/components/ui/button. Desk CTAs default to cornerClass('surface'). Scan-station chrome that must sit edge-to-edge passes radius flush — never a rounded-* literal.
Button.law: docs/roadmap/MASTER.md · docs/roadmap/LOOP_PROMPT.md · docs/operations-studio/Full Code Base Upgrade/03-DESIGN-LANGUAGE-2026.md — 'canonical Button ... never hand-roll'. Operator 2026-08-31: two Buttons, two jobs.

button.useWhen: shadcn, 21st.dev, new composed chrome, asChild trigger, quiet bar control, overlay chrome, shadcn-lane, primitive button
button.doNot: Not the house CTA. Ops actions take `Button` from @/design-system/primitives/Button. Compose new 21st.dev / shadcn-lane work from this file. House colour tokens, never bg-primary. Do not hand-roll the cva / Radix Slot structure.
button.law: src/components/ui/button.tsx — shadcn/new-york structure, house colour. Operator 2026-08-31: shadcn primitives are the compose base for new 21st.dev work.

OmnichannelComposerDock.useWhen: composer dock outline, text entry shell, prompt outline, raised composer card (not the full station mouth)
OmnichannelComposerDock.doNot: Do not mount this alone as a station mouth. Omni Composer / station composer / scan station mouth means StationComposerHost (dock + ComposerModeRow). Raw dock = incomplete mouth (no caption row, no context ring). Do not invent a second composer shell. Soft corner is COMPOSER_SHELL_CORNER only. Raised chrome owns elevationClass('raised') at z-raised — never overflow-hidden a parent around this shell (that shears the drop shadow). weldTop exists only to share a silhouette with WeldedFeedbackPanel — not a caption band or a second card.
OmnichannelComposerDock.law: Operator 2026-08-24: one composer outline. Operator 2026-08-31: dock is the raised card; mode row is the sibling under the outline. Operator 2026-08-31 (scan-out): saying Omni Composer and mounting only this file is a fork of the station mouth.

AssistantFabHost.useWhen: floating AI composer, assistant circle, Ask FAB, mobile assistant, global chat panel, bottom-right Sparkles
AssistantFabHost.doNot: DELETED 2026-09-02. Ask is a StationComposerHost mode, inline in the page. Do not resurrect a FAB, Dialog, Popover, or RightRail Ask occupant. Do not mount a second StationComposerHost on a scan station.
AssistantFabHost.law: StationComposerHost Ask mode. Operator 2026-09-02: no popover, no double mouth.

StationComposerHost.useWhen: station composer, unbox composer, ticket composer, ask composer, scan-station input, plus-button dock, omni composer, station mouth, floor scan mouth, dumb station composer, scan-out composer, gun station notes, incoming add extract composer, paste PO screenshot, assistant ask, AI agent working set
StationComposerHost.doNot: Do not invent a second station dock or a *NotesComposer wrapping OmnichannelComposerDock. Do not mount raw OmnichannelComposerDock for a scan station. Dumb / gun-only stations keep showModeRow and set showModeFaces={false} — never showModeRow={false} to hide Unbox|Ticket (that deletes the context ring). Faces-off still paints Ask. Modes are Unbox|Ticket|Ask. Plus is circular (composer shell radius). Do not add Notes or Location as modes. Do not weld the caption into the dock. Host floor is bg-surface-card + COMPOSER_SHELL_CORNER; elevation lives only on OmnichannelComposerDock. Prefer a thin adapter (commit routing only) over redesigning the mouth. Incoming add mounts this at the walk foot — do not replace it with a flush TextField bar. Do not paint `bg-transparent` or extra footer `pb-*` around the Incoming mount (that reads as empty pad under + / Add). Staff reaction on this mouth is WeldedFeedbackPanel on the `reaction` slot — never a second caption band, toast, or Popover. Ask is inline above this dock (ComposerAskStage) — never a FAB, Dialog, or nested StationComposerHost.
StationComposerHost.law: StationComposerHost file header. Operator 2026-08-30: unbox + ticket, one row, rounded plus. Operator 2026-08-31: white COMPOSER_SHELL_CORNER floor under modes; dock z-raised over caption z-base. Operator 2026-08-31 (scan-out): dumb station = same host, faces off, ring on, ring opens Displays. Operator 2026-09-01: Incoming add extract uses the same host under TriageScrollLayout cards. Operator 2026-09-02: Incoming extract eval is `pnpm run eval:station scan-out` (critiqueExtra + mouth tripwire), not overlay cohort. Operator 2026-09-02: ds_contract jobs about feedback / reaction / receive confirm on this mouth rank WeldedFeedbackPanel first. Operator 2026-09-02: Ask is the third mode; one mouth; desks fall back only when no station host is mounted.

WeldedFeedbackPanel.useWhen: staff reaction on the composer, what just happened, what to do next, look at the composer, process this feedback, live mouth update throughout the day, feedback above composer, composer feedback, composer reaction, reaction from the composer, status above composer, weldTop, welded stack, station scan feedback, receive confirm, Zoho inventory received, welded composer hinge, caption hinge, composer accessory stage, seller message refine, claim type above composer, in-flight receive, scan station status on the mouth
WeldedFeedbackPanel.doNot: Do not hand-roll a sunken caption band, a second card above StationComposerHost, a toast in the corner, or a matchWidth Popover for status hinged to the compose shell. Do not fork a new hinge / caption / toast — staff look HERE all day for what to process. Receive confirm, seller paste, link, and claim type all encode into THIS panel (steps = the one truncated line; children = disclosure or disclose=always body). Mount on StationComposerHost via `reaction` (any mode) or `ticketAccessory` (Ticket). Pair with OmnichannelComposerDock weldTop + WeldedStack. ComposerAccessoryStage is a disclose=always wrapper only. Dockless workbench feedback (no composer) stays InlineActionFeedbackCard. Do not import this from receiving/workspace — that path is deleted.
WeldedFeedbackPanel.law: src/components/composer/WeldedFeedbackPanel.tsx. Operator 2026-08-21: receive welds to the notes composer. Operator 2026-09-02: every composer-hinged staff update uses this shell. Operator 2026-09-02: moved out of receiving — this is the staff SoT for mouth reaction, catalog home staff mouth reaction. ds_contract force-ranks this id for feedback/reaction/confirm sitting on StationComposerHost.

ComposerAccessoryStage.useWhen: disclose always claim accessory wrapper around WeldedFeedbackPanel
ComposerAccessoryStage.doNot: Do not add chrome, a second caption band, or a new panel. This file only mounts WeldedFeedbackPanel with disclose=always. Status, receive confirm, and seller refine encode on WeldedFeedbackPanel.
ComposerAccessoryStage.law: src/components/composer/ComposerAccessoryStage.tsx. Operator 2026-09-02: thin wrapper — not a second SoT.

TextField.useWhen: floating label field, scan bar cell, flush industrial input, edge-to-edge text entry
TextField.doNot: Do not mount appearance=flush on a desk record walk (exceptions, Labels, Incoming add). Flush floating-label cells are scan-station / kiosk edge-to-edge chrome. Desk forms use Label + Input from ui/* with triagePanelControl inside cornerClass('surface') cards. Default (rounded) TextField is the non-flush house field — still not a substitute for the exceptions Label+Input recipe on triage walks.
TextField.law: src/design-system/primitives/TextField.tsx + src/design-system/tokens/desk-stage.ts. Operator 2026-09-01: flush field = scan stations; desk walks = surface cards.

ComposerModeRow.useWhen: unbox ticket ask mode row, composer caption, station mode switcher, composer procedure ring, context ring, dumb station bottom row, showModeFaces false
ComposerModeRow.doNot: Do not put Unbox|Ticket|Ask inside the dock outline. Do not give this row elevationClass — flat bg-surface-card plate at z-base so the dock's raised shadow falls across the labels. Same COMPOSER_SHELL_CORNER as the dock. Ask is the third mode. Do not omit this row on a dumb station — hide Unbox|Ticket with showModeFaces={false} and keep Ask plus the bottom-right context / procedure ring. Never a popover Ask.
ComposerModeRow.law: src/components/composer/ComposerModeRow.tsx. Operator 2026-08-31: caption sibling under the outline. Operator 2026-08-31 (scan-out): showModeFaces={false} keeps spacer + ring bottom-right. Operator 2026-09-02: Ask face stays when faces are off.

badge.useWhen: shadcn badge, 21st.dev badge, status chip, count chip, tag, pill label on a row, primitive badge
badge.doNot: Do not hand-roll a rounded-full span with a hex background. Glyph + text together — never colour alone. Copyable identifiers are CopyChip, not this. Domain status strings are StatusBadge. Compose new 21st.dev / shadcn-lane work from this file. House colour tokens, never bg-primary.
badge.law: src/components/ui/badge.tsx — shadcn structure, house colour. Pin key is the filename id (`badge`), not `Badge`.

input.useWhen: shadcn input, 21st.dev input, labeled field, overlay field, primitive input
input.doNot: Not the flush industrial bar cell — that is TextField from @/design-system/primitives/TextField. Pair with `label` from @/components/ui/label. House colour tokens, never bg-primary. Do not hand-roll a <input> on a shadcn-lane surface.

useOptimisticMutation.useWhen: edit, save, update, patch, rename, toggle, inline save, optimistic write, mutation after user edit, save a field
useOptimisticMutation.doNot: Do not await the server before the UI changes. Do not call useMutation or useResourceMutation for an inline edit. Do not import toast from sonner. This hook paints the cache first, persists, and on failure rolls back and toast.error(why) via @/lib/toast (AppToaster, bottom-right). Creates / fire-and-forget with no cached row still use useResourceMutation.
useOptimisticMutation.law: Operator 2026-08-30 — edits are optimistic; the paint is the feedback; failure is a bottom-right toast.

ProgressBar.useWhen: progress meter, completion bar, stage progress, percent done, N of M, goal against actual
ProgressBar.doNot: Do not animate width, height, or position — the fill is a scaleX transform with transformOrigin:'left' and w-full, gated by useReducedMotion. Law M1 bans layout tweens; transform was struck from that ban 2026-08-25, so the fill is legal only in that form. Duration is framerDuration.progressFill (100ms), never an inline literal. Progression is a COUNT, never a pointer position: pass satisfied-required-steps over total-required, so a pointer sitting on step 5 of 8 does not render 5/8.
ProgressBar.law: docs/warehouse-os/PROGRESSION-INTERVIEW-LEDGER.md — PG12 (segmented squares + a scaleX fill; M1 stands unamended), PG6 (percent-done is a count, never a position), PD1 (this file's width tween was the violation).

ProcedureDeck.useWhen: station work surface, procedure steps, step column, work list, guided procedure, unbox steps, the surface an operator works a station from
ProcedureDeck.doNot: Do not gate capture on the active step. Evidence claims the step it belongs to, so the pointer is a HINT about what to capture next, never an authority that rejects input — scanning what step 5 wants while the pointer sits on step 2 satisfies step 5, and steps 3-4 stay open and unticked. Do not auto-complete the steps in between. Every step stays mounted from the first frame (existing invariant 1) — that is what makes a jumped-past open step visible without a scroll, so do not virtualize or collapse the list.
ProcedureDeck.law: docs/warehouse-os/PROGRESSION-INTERVIEW-LEDGER.md — PG6 (evidence claims its own step; progression is non-linear), PG3 (evidence advances the pointer).

StepStateBadge.useWhen: step state mark, procedure step box, done/skipped/pending mark, checklist square
StepStateBadge.doNot: Do not make it clickable and do not render a rounded-full dot. A step is evidence-derived — a square that clicks to tick reintroduces the banned hand-ticked checklist. `skipped` keeps the chevron and never the check: a skip is a recorded waiver that a person looked and moved past, not a claim the work happened, and a required step skipped this way carries a deviation reason. One mark serves both ProcedureChecklist and ProcedureDeck; do not fork it per view.
StepStateBadge.law: File docblock (shape + evidence-derived). docs/warehouse-os/PROGRESSION-INTERVIEW-LEDGER.md — PG3 (evidence advances; tick is the fallback), PG8 (a skipped required step is a recorded deviation), PG1 (one derivation at two altitudes).

calendar.useWhen: calendar, date picker, day picker, month grid, shadcn calendar, 21st.dev calendar, react-day-picker
calendar.doNot: Do not import 'react-day-picker/style.css'. This file names EVERY key in react-day-picker's UI enum, so no rdp-* class is emitted and the stylesheet is dead weight — while it was imported, the keys the old component missed (root, weeks, chevron) inherited library styling and .rdp-chevron{fill:var(--rdp-accent-color)} filled the nav chevron's stroked path into a solid blue triangle. Do not write data-[range-start=true] / data-[range-end=true] / data-[range-middle=true] chains: this repo is on react-day-picker v10, which emits none of those attributes — that is v9, and most shadcn range snippets in circulation are v9 or v8. Do not put raw text-blue-* inside an arbitrary variant ([&>button]: or hover:); the dark-scheme remap in styles/globals.css only rewrites the BARE class, so it goes dark-on-dark — use a themed token. Do not drop relative or w-fit from the root, and do not simplify nav to inset-x-0 top-0: the p-3 root makes those offsets wrong by 12px vertically and 16px horizontally. Range picking is calendar-range-select, not this with mode="range" hand-styled. A full field (trigger + popover + Apply) is DateRangePickerField or DateRangePickerPill, not this bare. Do not mount this as an inline table date editor. Slot-table ship-by / due date / pick a date in a cell is DateRangePickerField variant="compact" (not variant=range).
calendar.law: src/components/ui/calendar.tsx — shadcn/new-york lineage on react-day-picker v10, house tokens. Operator 2026-08-31: one calendar primitive; src/design-system/components/Calendar.tsx was deleted and all six consumers moved here.

calendar-range-select.useWhen: date range, range picker, from-to dates, period picker, week range, filter by date range, range calendar, start and end date
calendar-range-select.doNot: Do not hand-style a range on `calendar` — this file is the only place the range track is defined. range_middle must keep Tailwind's `!` suffix: in v10 a middle day is BOTH selected and range_middle and the two class strings land on the same cell, so equal specificity would let stylesheet order pick the winner. Do not move the endpoint pill off `selected` onto range_start/range_end — a half-picked range (from set, to open) sets only `selected`, because v10 requires both endpoints before it marks the range. Do not add a preset row above it; the four period chips were removed 2026-08-31 for restating the calendar and forcing the popover wider than the grid. This is the bare calendar — the trigger + popover + Apply field is DateRangePickerField variant="range", and the workbench-chrome pill is DateRangePickerPill. Do not drop this bare grid into a table cell. Cell / ship-by / due date is DateRangePickerField variant="compact".
calendar-range-select.law: src/components/ui/calendar-range-select.tsx — layers only range_start / range_end / range_middle over `calendar`. Operator 2026-08-31: ported from 21st.dev, retranslated from react-day-picker v9 to v10.

DateRangePickerField.useWhen: inline date edit, ship-by date, due date, slot table date, pick a date in a cell, date under status, calendar date range display, date range field, replace input type=date, pick a date, single date
DateRangePickerField.doNot: Do not use InlineEditableValue for a date. Do not mount a native input type=date. Do not drop bare calendar or calendar-range-select into a table cell — those are the grid, this is the field. DateRangePickerPill is workbench header chrome only. variant="range" is the filter (presets + Apply + X, year in the face). variant="compact" is one civil day: calendar only, click commits, no X, no year, face is never blank. Slot-table ship-by is compact. On the compound DATES cell BOTH lines are this field — order date on top, ship-by under it — and a line the surface cannot write mounts the same field `disabled`, never a plain text twin. The DATES cell passes leadingGlyph={Hash} on the order line and leadingGlyph={CalendarClock} on ship-by; the deadline glyph inherits the age ink and does not swap when late. Form compact mounts keep the default calendar. The ship-by line passes `faceLabel` and paints its AGE (`2d late` / `1m late`), with the civil day on the hover; do not print the date on that trigger and do not add a second inline date control for it. Do not hand-roll a CompoundShipByEditor or a click-to-native-date control.
DateRangePickerField.law: src/design-system/components/DateRangePickerField.tsx. Operator 2026-09-01: slot-table / ship-by / inline date edit is variant=compact. Filter ranges stay variant=range. Operator 2026-09-04: the DATES cell paints both dates with this one field, and the ship-by face is the age, not the day.

InlineEditableValue.useWhen: inline text edit, pencil edit, click to retype a string, rename in place
InlineEditableValue.doNot: Not for dates. Ship-by, due date, and any inline date edit is DateRangePickerField variant="compact" (click commits, no X, no year).

DataTable.useWhen: data table, spreadsheet, grid, table, columns, column header, sortable column, fields picker, row selection, find row, filter a list, queue display, worklist, triage queue, desk queue, backlog, exceptions queue, port a table onto a page, add a data table, register a table, new backend table, table engine, adapter for a table, reuse the slot table for another entity, one table SoT
DataTable.doNot: Do NOT hand-roll a per-family `*-grid-layout.ts` column array plus a `*GridRow.tsx` with a switch over column keys — that is a second table, and this repo has one. A column this grid does not print yet is a SLOT BINDING in a field catalog (@/lib/tables/field-catalog/*) resolved by the layout cascade and materialized by materializeTracks; add the field, do not fork the display. Do NOT register a new entityFamily / TableId / TableSurfaceBinding just because a row shape carries facts the current sheet lacks — adapt the row instead (see exceptionRowToQueueRow / cagedRecordToQueueRow) and mount the family's existing spreadsheet hook (useOrdersSpreadsheet for every outbound lane). No page supplies chrome: search, filter, tabs, counts and the fields picker are DATA props, never ReactNode slots, and there is no renderColumnHeader to fork with. renderRow / renderGroup stay render props only because a CELL is domain code. On a desk, mount with DESK_TABLE_SURFACE_CLASS — edge-to-edge inside desk-page-stage; do NOT wrap this in rounded-lg, border, or shadow (the card shell clips corners via overflow-hidden). Selection tabs that merely narrow the same row set are FILTERS and belong in the one filter control; `all` is the absence of a filter, never a tab. The URL is the state — search, filter, active tab and sort are controlled by the caller and parked in the URL. Do not mount FilterRefinementBar (or hunt tiles, or a second toolbar) above this table — DataTableFilterMenu always sits to the right of SearchField (DATA_TABLE_FILTER_IDLE when a family has no facets). Every painted DATA column header is click-to-sort (`SLOT_TABLE_PAINT_LAW.headerSort` / `isSlotTableChromeTrack`). Never leave Image, Status, Amount, Order, Item, or a bound status:N header inert. Chrome only: select, actions/action, _fill. Do not build a *GridView / *GridHost / *GridRow for a new entity. A table is a REGISTRATION: field catalog + resolver + row adapter + registry entry, and zero new .tsx. Register to the ENTITY, not to the page — scope, lane lock and layout are parameters of the mount, so one dataset shown on three pages is ONE registration. The descriptor may add DATA (fields, widths, capabilities, tier) and never BEHAVIOR: no render props, no per-family cell, no override hook. displayType is a CLOSED vocabulary owned by the engine — a family adds FIELDS, only the engine adds TYPES (and then for everyone). If a mount needs behaviour the engine lacks, the engine gains it or the mount does without.
DataTable.law: src/components/tables/DataTable.tsx + src/components/tables/table-surface-binding.ts. docs/todo/one-table-sot-teardown-HANDOFF.md — thirty per-desk table displays were torn down on 2026-08-29 for exactly this. Operator 2026-08-31, after an agent hand-rolled a grid for /shipping/exceptions: "You must use the one data table component, the slot table, the linear host." Operator 2026-09-01: click any data header to sort; freeze is not unsortable. Law file: src/lib/tables/slot-table-header-sort.ts. src/lib/tables/table-engine-law.ts. Tripwire: src/lib/tables/table-engine-law.test.ts (cohort slot-table). Operator 2026-09-04: "it should be pinned under one source of truth ... so it will never fork again".

NonlinearTableHost.useWhen: mount a table, table host, grid host, render rows into a sheet, virtualized table body
NonlinearTableHost.doNot: Do not mount this directly from a page. A page mounts DataTable, which owns the one chrome row above this host; reaching past it is how a desk grows its own toolbar. A family's glue (useOrdersSpreadsheet and its siblings) resolves the feed bag — records, groups, row renderers, sort — and the page spreads it.
NonlinearTableHost.law: src/components/tables/NonlinearTableHost.tsx. One host, one chrome, every desk.

materialize-tracks.useWhen: add a column, new column, show a field on the table, column model, grid tracks, slot layout, slot binding, fields menu, per-staff column preferences, organization column layout
materialize-tracks.doNot: Do not write a column array by hand for a surface on this engine. Track keys are SLOT INDICES (`status:1`, `subtitle:2`), never field ids, so rebinding a slot keeps every width and staff preference keyed to that slot. Declare the FACT as a field in @/lib/tables/field-catalog/* and bind it; the materializer turns bindings into tracks. `makeDescriptor` must be a module-level reference, never an inline arrow — LedgerGridSurface memoizes on it and a fresh identity rebuilds the state engine's column list every render.
materialize-tracks.law: src/lib/tables/materialize-tracks.ts + src/lib/tables/slot-layout.ts + src/components/tables/useSlotTableLayout.ts. docs/kill-list/07-slot-table-hand-models.md — layout encoded as a second product table is what the Wave-1 hand-model kill removed.

LabelFacePreview.useWhen: printed sticker, label preview, 2x1 label, carton label, unit label, inline edit label face, sticker corners, platform type on label, scan-station label
LabelFacePreview.doNot: Do not hand-roll a second sticker preview or a per-station hit map. Mount LabelFacePreview (print-faithful iframe) and pass slotHits from useLabelFaceReceivingSlots (carton: platform·type, date, condition, corner) or useLabelFaceProductSlots (unit: title, condition, color). Overlay is LabelFaceSlotOverlay — flush to the paper, never a padded wrap. Platform / type menus are LabelPlatformTypeMenu (sentence case, catalogIdentityDot). WorkspaceLabelPreviewCard / LabelPreviewCard / UnboxLabelPreview are the hosts; a new scan station that shows a label uses those, not a fork. Do not use the shadcn `label` primitive for this job.
LabelFacePreview.law: src/components/labels/LabelFacePreview.tsx + LabelFaceSlotOverlay.tsx + LabelFaceReceivingSlots.tsx + LabelFaceProductSlots.tsx. Operator 2026-08-31: one sticker, pinpoint slots, every scan station.

LabelFaceSlotOverlay.doNot: Do not invent a second overlay. Corners are a short edge row (13%); notes are only the middle flex-1 band. Host is LabelFacePreview slotHits.
LabelFaceSlotOverlay.law: src/components/labels/LabelFaceSlotOverlay.tsx. Operator 2026-08-31: flush hits on the print-faithful face.

LabelPlatformTypeMenu.useWhen: label platform type menu, carton top-left, platform then type, classify dots on label
LabelPlatformTypeMenu.doNot: Do not fork a second platform/type picker for the sticker. One popover, two lists; a pick does not dismiss. Sentence case via chipLabel + sentenceCaseLabel; dots via catalogIdentityDot. Click-off / Escape closes.
LabelPlatformTypeMenu.law: src/components/labels/LabelPlatformTypeMenu.tsx. Operator 2026-08-31: SoT for the carton top-left.

TicketComposer.useWhen: ticket reply, helpdesk reply, zendesk comment, internal note, public reply, claim body, file a ticket, support composer, cc a colleague, attach a photo to a ticket
TicketComposer.doNot: Do not hand-roll a ticket composer. This is the ONE mouth for a helpdesk comment on every surface — /support console, the station Ticket mode, any future ticket tab. It owns the whole grammar together: Internal|Public on the action bar right of `+` (never inside `+`), Cc above the draft on Public only, `+` = photo attach (Browse library · Upload file, flat and untitled), and a LABELLED commit (File ticket → / Update ticket) — never a bare return arrow, because this control files a helpdesk ticket or posts to a customer-visible thread. `@` means Cc and only Cc; it has never meant attach-context since 2026-08-30. Send through buildComposerReplyVars — never assemble SupportReplyVars by hand, or the station and the console drift on signing, emailCcs and photoIds again.
TicketComposer.law: src/components/composer/TicketComposer.tsx + useTicketComposer.ts. Operator 2026-08-31: one SoT composer, ported to /support; the hand-rolled SupportChatComposer was deleted with it.

useTicketComposer.useWhen: ticket composer state, reply draft state, cc state, photo staging for a ticket, ticket send payload
useTicketComposer.doNot: Do not re-derive this state in a host. It owns draft, channel, Cc chips + the half-typed address, photo staging, the `+` tree and the send. A host that keeps its own copy is how the console and the station diverged the first time.
useTicketComposer.law: Operator 2026-08-31: the behaviour is the SoT, not just the chrome.

ComposerTicketCcStrip.useWhen: cc, email cc, add a colleague to a reply, audience of a public reply
ComposerTicketCcStrip.doNot: Public replies only — an internal note is never emailed, so it has no audience to name. Never render it for an internal note, and never send emailCcs on one (resolveComposerCcPayload answers undefined, not []). The `@` button focuses the email field; it is not a context-attach menu.
ComposerTicketCcStrip.law: src/lib/composer/ticket-cc.ts is the rule set. Operator 2026-08-30: @ is audience, + is attach.

ComposerDrillMenu.useWhen: composer plus menu, add to message, attach, drill menu, submenu in a composer
ComposerDrillMenu.doNot: No DropdownMenuSub flyouts on a station — a glove on a mounted screen has nothing to hover with; submenus PUSH into the same panel with a back control. No title row on the root page. No height tween between stack pages. Reset the stack on close.
ComposerDrillMenu.law: Operator 2026-08-30/31: in-panel stack, no root title.

Do not re-type visibility/inert/zIndex.panel in a workspace — call idleBrowseLayerProps and overlayPaneStyle. Do not delete those calls to silence ds_critique. Operator 2026-09-02: hide/stack is the helper, not a per-station style string. Display eval is slot-table; shell eval is `pnpm run eval:station <id>`.

idle-overlay.useWhen: idle overlay, browse under focus, visibility hidden idle, overlay pane stack, zIndex.panel overlay, station swap shell hide
idle-overlay.doNot: Do not re-type visibility/inert/pointer-events-none/zIndex.panel in a floor workspace. Call idleBrowseLayerProps(overlayOpen, className) on the browse layer and overlayPaneStyle(hardCut) on the focused pane.
idle-overlay.law: src/design-system/motion/idle-overlay.ts. Operator 2026-09-02: the overlay contract is this API.

roles.doNot: Do not pick a duration or a framerPresence literal for a job that already has a role. overlay swap is motionRole.swap.scan or .focus. Do not add a role to tweak timing — change the preset.

station-skins.useWhen: scan station theme, station skin, porcelain packing bench, station color, applyStationSkin, mill industrial coal
station-skins.doNot: Do not hex-fill a well or fork a packing-bench class on one station. Color is a STATION_SKINS row; wells consume STATION_SCAN_* from @/components/station/scan-depth. Query ds_tokens({ axis: 'station-skin' }). Industrial is the absence of data-station-skin. Grain and bevel width are station-depth.

ItemRecordMobileMeta.useWhen: mobile to-ship qty condition notes, phone item record facts, qty condition notes cluster, handheld order card meta

ItemRecordQtyBadge.useWhen: item quantity badge, expected qty, counted over expected, phone to-ship quantity
ItemRecordQtyBadge.doNot: Do not hand-roll a qty span. Expected-only sales orders paint the number; counted/expected paints n/m. Mount inside ItemRecordMobileMeta on the phone card.

MobileScanOutCamera.useWhen: mobile scan out, phone scan out, handheld ship confirm, /m/scan-out, phone camera scan window, camera viewfinder window, mobile dock scan, scan out on a phone, mobile scan tape, scanned out list on phone
MobileScanOutCamera.doNot: Do not mount a text field, a ThemedStationScanBar / ScanInput, or StationComposerHost on this screen — the window IS the camera and arms itself on mount (operator 2026-09-04). Do not mount a second camera anywhere on the page: two getUserMedia streams contend. Do not stack chrome above or below the video — torch, state pill and the running foot are overlays on it. Keep the viewfinder mask: white shipping labels wash out every un-scrimmed overlay. Reticle brackets are the accent, never white. Do not square the corners — this surface takes the MOBILE_SCAN_* family from tokens/radius.ts (window 24 -> card 16 -> row 12), which is the ONE departure from flush-square and is scoped to handheld scan surfaces only. Do not reach for those tokens on a desk, a scan-station well, a DataTable or a workbench plate. The tape is fed from useScanOutStation's onSettled (every settle, arrival-ordered), never from `active` — a tape built off `active` drops confirms that were overtaken in flight.
MobileScanOutCamera.law: src/components/mobile/redesign/MobileScanOutCamera.tsx + MobileScanOut.tsx + mobile-scan-out-tape.ts; corners in src/design-system/tokens/radius.ts (MOBILE_SCAN_WINDOW_CORNER / _CARD_ / _ROW_ / _RETICLE_). Operator 2026-09-04: a phone is not a desk — every surface floats, so the handheld scan screens round off while the desk stays flush. Same operator call: camera-only window, no keyboard cell; a re-read of a label that already left reads SCANNED OUT like any other, and the STAMP (just now vs 1h) is what separates them.

SelectionActionBar.useWhen: bulk action, row action, selection verb, selection action bar, mark as, undo, action bar, table action, three-dot row menu, scan out in bulk, bulk actions, add an action to a page, add an action to a table, per-lane actions
SelectionActionBar.doNot: Do not declare a SelectionAction at a PAGE or a mount — verbs are declared ONCE in the family's verb catalog (VERB_CATALOG_MODULES in src/lib/tables/table-engine-law.ts) and BOUND per surface. Do not add a per-lane hardcoded action key list: a verb names the FIELD it writes and is offered wherever the mounted layout resolves that field. Direction (do / undo / already-done) comes from row STATE, never from the route — "Mark scanned out" and "Undo scan-out" are ONE reversible verb with two directions, not two verbs on two pages. A mixed selection RESOLVES (majority direction, remainder named in disabledReason), it does not hide. Bulk is a cardinality, not a mode: the row ⋮ menu is the same catalog at n=1. Gate with enabled(rows) + disabledReason, never by branching on the page.
SelectionActionBar.law: src/lib/tables/table-engine-law.ts (TABLE_ENGINE_LAW.verbsBindToFields) + src/lib/selection/selection-actions.tsx. Tripwire: src/lib/tables/table-engine-law.test.ts under `pnpm run eval:cohort slot-table`. Operator 2026-09-04: one pinned SoT for actions, not one per page.

mobile-display.useWhen: mobile button size, phone control size, touch target, tap target, 44pt, apple hig, mobile font size, mobile type scale, /m page, handheld station, how big should this button be on mobile, mobile spacing
mobile-display.doNot: Do not size a phone control by its touch floor. Apple's 44x44 is the HIT REGION and the HIG says the visible control may be smaller — paint small, expand the hit area with padding. The ladder is MOBILE_CONTROL_LADDER: inline 28/44, row 36/44, cta 44/44, one cta per surface. Never size="lg" (h-14 = 56px) on /m. Never text-role-micro on /m — 10px is under Apple's 11pt legibility floor; the floor is text-role-eyebrow. At most two text-role-* per mobile component (MOBILE_MAX_TYPE_ROLES_PER_FILE): hierarchy on a phone is weight and ground, not a third size. A new /m surface must join MOBILE_DISPLAY_COHORT or the tripwire fails.
mobile-display.law: src/lib/mobile/mobile-display-cohort.ts (SoT) + mobile-display-cohort.test.ts (tripwire, asserted on every member). CI: scripts/ci/check-mobile-display-law.mjs (blocking) and scripts/ci/check-law-checksums.mjs (the law file is hashed into docs/eval/law-checksums.json so it cannot be quietly relaxed). Eval: pnpm run eval:cohort mobile-display, and eval:station scan-out runs the tripwire. Sources: Apple HIG 'UI Design Dos and Don'ts' (44x44 controls; text at least 11 points), Apple HIG Buttons (hit region vs visible size), WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 (24x24 CSS px, AA). Operator 2026-09-05: 28/36/44, Apple rules win.

ProviderSignInButton.useWhen: sign in page, OAuth button, Google sign in, Apple sign in, identity provider button, auth page composition, credential form order, phone QR sign in
ProviderSignInButton.doNot: Provider buttons (Google, Apple, …) are the first interactive section of the sign-in card, unconditionally above the email/password form — never gated behind an auth-method toggle or a drawer state. Phone/QR sign-in is a persistent bottom action on the same card, never tucked into a secondary 'More' menu. Card order is fixed: provider buttons, then the credential form, then QR/phone sign-in.
ProviderSignInButton.law: src/app/signin/page.tsx + src/components/auth/ProviderSignInButton.tsx. Operator 2026-09-04: first pass gated the provider buttons; operator repeated the order explicitly — providers must appear above the sign-in email entry. Same session moved phone QR sign-in out of the 'More' drawer into a persistent bottom action.

radiant-lines.useWhen: auth page backdrop, sign-in page background, marketing background decoration, low-density line texture
radiant-lines.doNot: Restrained, low-density backdrop layer only — must never raise visual weight above the primary card it sits behind. Not a general-purpose background for operator desks or scan stations.
radiant-lines.law: src/components/ui/radiant-lines.tsx (shadcn registry: @23rd/radiant-lines). Operator 2026-09-04: installed for the sign-in page backdrop specifically, kept restrained so the auth card stays the focal point.

role-eyebrow.useWhen: uppercase tracking-wide label, all-caps header, eyebrow text, table column header caption, short static field label
role-eyebrow.doNot: Do not bind uppercase / tracking-wide styling to a live or frequently-re-read value (a counter, 'Showing N of M', a roster key, a running total) or to a string longer than about three words — all-caps is legible for a short static label, not for a number that changes or a sentence. Confirmed regressions: UnshippedTable.tsx 'Showing 200 of 847', OrderRailShell.tsx roster keys, MobileScanOutRow.tsx / MobileScanOut.tsx full-sentence eyebrows.
role-eyebrow.law: src/design-system/tokens/typography/presets.ts (role-eyebrow) + families.ts. Operator, multiple sessions: eyebrow caps belong on short static labels (table headers, rail labels) only, never on a value that changes or reads as a sentence.

GlobalDetailStackHost.useWhen: record tile navigation, detail stack panel, close vs back button on a tile, order or unit detail opened from a global action, tile band
GlobalDetailStackHost.doNot: A stack opened straight from a global action (assistant recents, global search) owes no Back — close only, top-right. A stack routed through an index keeps Back. Do not add a Back control to a directly-opened tile, and do not drop Close from an indexed one. Identity / context info (who, what, where) surfaces once in GlobalHeader — never re-stated on the tile itself.
GlobalDetailStackHost.law: src/components/detail-stacks/GlobalDetailStackHost.tsx (file header: panels own their band — Back · title · host close cell). Operator 2026-08-25: tiles get a close button top-right, never a back button, for anything not routed through an index; the global header is the one place identity/context lives.

CommandBar.useWhen: cmd-k, command palette, global search shortcut, quick access, jump to page
CommandBar.doNot: Results never surface past chat / agent sessions — Recents in MasterNav is the one place session history lives. Do not fold chat or agent history into cmd-k result groups.
